landing.title: DotaDraft
landing.tagline: Draft five heroes. Get honest analysis. Fight for the win.
landing.pitch: DotaDraft is a browser strategy game built around the Dota 2 draft — pick a team, get a real evaluation of its strengths and weaknesses, then send it into Battle Mode against another player's draft or a professional lineup. No accounts, no downloads — just the draft.

draft.title: Draft five heroes
draft.text: Five rounds, five candidates each. Live synergy highlighting shows which pick fits what you already have — and which one fights it.

evaluate.title: Get an honest read
evaluate.text: Your lineup is scored on synergy, tempo, control, scaling and more, each axis ranked against 50,000 unique Ancient + Divine drafts from OpenDota so a number actually means something.

battle.title: Send it into battle
battle.text: Face another player's committed draft or a professional lineup. Win or lose, with a confidence tier — never a fake precise percentage.

about.title: How This Works
about.intro: DotaDraft isn't a full match simulator — there's no lane phase, no item builds, no player skill. It's an honest statistical model built on real match data, and it's upfront about what that can and can't tell you.
about.evaluationText: Your draft gets scored on things like synergy, tempo, control, and scaling — each axis is calibrated against real win-rate data from thousands of matches, not just a hand-picked formula.
about.battleText: Your draft faces another lineup. The outcome uses DotaDraft axes and tags — and also real OpenDota hero win rates plus how those heroes actually perform against each other, not only in-app stats.
about.ceilingText: A draft alone can't fully predict a real match — execution matters more than any stat sheet. We'd rather be honest about that uncertainty than pretend to false precision.

story.title: How the match may have unfolded
story.disclaimer: A read from this fight's lanes, pairs, and axes — not a reconstructed replay.
story.turnerLine: {{turner}} is the one who turns a lost fight — the save, not the first jump in.
story.openingLaneHook: It actually breaks in the {{openingLane}}: {{openingPairHero}} into {{openingPairVs}} ({{openingPairWinRate}}%) is a real hole, not just a lane score.
story.carryLateMatchup: Late, the argument is {{myCarry}} vs {{theirCarry}} — {{lateMatchupWinner}} owns that matchup ({{carryWinRate}}%).
story.carryScale: The longer this lives, the more dangerous {{scaleLeader}} gets.
story.openingAhead: {{winner}} takes the lanes {{winnerLanes}}–{{loserLanes}}. {{driver}} is first into every fight — that's whose tempo the opening is on.
story.openingComeback: The lanes went {{loserLanes}}–{{winnerLanes}} against the side that still wins. {{driver}} is the one who has to drag the map back.
story.openingEven: Nobody takes the lanes clean. From here it's fights, and {{driver}} is the one who starts them.
story.openingUpset: The favorite closed the lanes {{winnerLanes}}–{{loserLanes}}. If this flips, it starts with who walks into the fights first: {{driver}}.
story.turningCatchCombo: {{posture}}{{matchupWinner}} gets onto {{matchupLoser}} ({{matchupWinRate}}%). {{comboA}} + {{comboB}} ({{comboWinRate}}%) is the pairing that actually wins games together — that's the turn.
story.turningCatch: {{posture}}{{matchupWinner}} gets onto {{matchupLoser}} ({{matchupWinRate}}%). That's the matchup the other side doesn't solve while it's on the map.
story.turningCombo: {{posture}}{{comboA}} + {{comboB}} ({{comboWinRate}}%) is not a vibe. Together they win games, and the turn is tied to that pair.
story.turningAxis: {{posture}}There's no pretty catch on the sheet. The winning side's real edge is {{topAxis}} — the thing the other draft doesn't answer.
story.turningUpsetHighSkill: {{swingHero}} is the kind of hero who steals games the sheet can't price. This one went the wrong way for the favorite.
story.conversionRoshanEarly: This is a tempo draft. The game they want ends in the {{roshanBand}} window — after that, they're playing against the other roster's late game.
story.conversionRoshanMid: Neither side has a sharp clock. The fight lives in the {{roshanBand}} window, where Roshan is the prize if someone can actually take the map.
story.conversionRoshanLate: This draft is playing for the {{roshanBand}} window. If the game gets there, the late game is the actual win condition.
story.finishHeld: The pre-fight read held. This was their game if they didn't give the clock away.
story.finishComeback: The lanes lied about the ending. They didn't win the lane phase — they won the game anyway.
story.finishUpset: The underdog closed it. The pre-fight favorite was supposed to be the story. They weren't.

teamfight.high: Expect this team to look for 5v5 fights around Roshan, high ground, and objective clusters rather than split-pushing.
teamfight.mid: It can hold its own in an even fight but shouldn't force a 5-man engagement blindly.
teamfight.low: Avoid grouping for even fights — pick-offs, split pushes, and disengaging from bad fights are the safer path here.

tempo.high: This is a fast-start draft that wants to contest the first Rune, force early lane swaps, and close the game before the 25-minute mark — real match data shows drafts like this see their win rate fall the longer the game runs.
tempo.mid: It can play either an early skirmish game or settle into a patient one depending on how the laning stage goes.
tempo.low: Avoid forcing early confrontations — this team wants to reach the 30+ minute mark, where real match data shows drafts like this actually turn their win rate around.

scaling.high: This team gets meaningfully stronger every ten minutes it survives — real match data shows drafts like this often start behind on win rate before 25 minutes and pull ahead past 40, so the priority is farming safely and denying Roshan/high-ground pushes rather than forcing action early.
scaling.mid: It scales reasonably but isn't a guaranteed late-game powerhouse — neither rushing nor stalling the game is a clear win condition on its own.
scaling.low: This team doesn't get much stronger with time and should look to end the game early — real match data shows the win-rate gap for drafts like this tends to widen the longer the game goes.

mobility.high: High mobility lets this team roam between lanes, collapse on isolated targets, and reposition out of bad fights quickly.
mobility.mid: It has some mobility tools but isn't especially map-mobile — rotations will be telegraphed.
mobility.low: Low mobility makes this team vulnerable to being caught out of position and slow to answer ganks on other lanes.

map_control.high: Strong warding and roaming presence should let this team see enemy rotations coming and set up their own ganks on the river and jungle entrances.
map_control.mid: Vision is about average — standard warding discipline on the high-ground cliffs will be needed to avoid getting caught.
map_control.low: Weak map control leaves this team blind to rotations — expect to get ganked in lane more than a typical draft.

objectives.high: This team pushes towers and barracks efficiently and should look to close games through map pressure rather than waiting for a decisive teamfight.
objectives.mid: It can take a tower when the opportunity is there but isn't built to siege on its own.
objectives.low: Weak at taking structures — this team should convert kills into picks rather than trying to push lanes after a fight.

saving.high: Strong healing and defensive tools should keep the team's priority targets alive through a bad initiation.
saving.mid: Some saving tools are available, but this team can't bail out every bad engagement — good positioning matters more than usual.
saving.low: Little in the way of healing or defensive cooldowns — a bad engagement or a blink initiation onto a core is likely to end in a death.

burst.high: This team can delete a priority target out of a fog-of-war initiation — a clean pick-off window is often lethal.
burst.mid: Some burst potential is there, but this team can't reliably one-shot a priority target through defensive items.
burst.low: Low burst damage means this team relies on sustained fighting and kiting rather than quick kills — expect longer fights.

control.high: Heavy disable chains let this team lock down a target through Black King Bar and dictate exactly when fights happen.
control.mid: Some disable is available, but not enough to fully control a fight on its own — timing initiations around cooldowns matters.
control.low: Light on disables — this team will struggle to lock down mobile or spell-immune targets and may lose fights to a clean BKB play.

durability.high: This team is tanky and hard to burst down, and can afford to front-line and body-block for the rest of the team in fights.
durability.mid: Moderate durability — this team can still be burst down by a focused-fire initiation.
durability.low: Fragile and vulnerable to burst — bad positioning near the enemy's initiators is likely to get someone deleted.

initiating.high: Strong initiation tools let this team pick exactly when and where a fight starts, catching the enemy team out of position on rotations.
initiating.mid: It can start some fights on its own terms, but lacks a single dedicated initiation threat to build a play around.
initiating.low: Weak initiation means this team will usually be reacting to the enemy's engage rather than dictating the fight themselves.

skirmish_rate.high: This team leans into risk — trading and dying for river/jungle skirmishes rather than playing it safe, which real match data links to a better actual win rate than a pure stat sheet would suggest.
skirmish_rate.mid: A moderate risk appetite — not purely passive, but not built around constant early trades either.
skirmish_rate.low: This team plays it safe and prioritizes efficient farm over trades — real data suggests that safety can come at the cost of actually winning.

camp_stacking.high: This team stacks jungle camps for each other — a supportive, resource-sharing playstyle real data links to a better actual win rate than a pure stat sheet would suggest.
camp_stacking.mid: Camps get stacked occasionally, without a game plan built around it.
camp_stacking.low: This team doesn't stack camps for each other — not necessarily a problem (efficient personal farmers score low here too), but the team isn't generating this kind of shared resource.

resource_efficiency.high: This team deals real damage without needing a large share of the team's gold to do it — priority farm can go to whichever hero needs it most instead of being locked to whoever hits hardest.
resource_efficiency.mid: Damage output is reasonably proportionate to farm priority — no strong efficiency edge either way.
resource_efficiency.low: This team's damage is expensive — it depends on a hero (or heroes) getting a large share of the team's resources first, so a slow start or contested farm hits harder here than for a more efficient draft.

win.fast: This is a draft that wants to win fast: force early lane swaps and skirmishes, take fights before 25 minutes, and avoid letting the game drag — it does not get meaningfully stronger with time.
win.patient: This is a patient draft: farm safely, avoid unnecessary risk in the laning stage, and let the game run past 35-40 minutes, where its late-game power actually shows up.
win.flexible: This draft has real flexibility in how the game is played — it can force an early lead off a fast start, or fall back on genuine late-game scaling if the opening does not go to plan.
win.neither: This draft has no strong forcing function in either direction — it does not want to rush the early game or stall for a late-game payoff, so small edges and picks have to be manufactured rather than relied on.
win.middle: This draft sits in the middle on both game speed and scaling — the win condition depends more on execution and picks than on a built-in early or late-game plan.

synergy.dampened: (real data shows this pairing underperforms expectations, weighted down)
synergy.none: No strong hero-to-hero synergies detected in this composition.
synergy.mobility: Multiple high-mobility heroes ({{heroes}}) enable pick-off plays.
synergy.realStrong: {{heroA}} + {{heroB}} have a strong real win rate together — outperforming what their individual strength alone would predict.
synergy.realWeak: {{heroA}} + {{heroB}} have a below-average real win rate together — underperforming what their individual strength alone would predict.

summary.high: This is a well-connected draft — the heroes' kits actively support one another.
summary.mid: This draft has some hero synergy, but the picks don't form a tightly connected game plan.
summary.low: This draft is fairly disconnected — the heroes don't strongly support each other's game plans.

pair.needs_setup_enables_engage: {{heroA}} (needs setup) + {{heroB}} (enables engage): initiation sets up pick-off/burst combos.
pair.needs_space_creates_space: {{heroB}} (creates space) supports {{heroA}} (needs space) to scale safely.
pair.needs_space_protects_allies: {{heroB}} (protects allies) helps keep {{heroA}} (needs space) alive while farming.
pair.enables_engage_amplifies_magic_damage: {{heroA}} (enables engage) sets up {{heroB}} (amplifies magic damage) for burst follow-up.
pair.enables_engage_amplifies_physical_damage: {{heroA}} (enables engage) sets up {{heroB}} (amplifies physical damage) for follow-up.
pair.wave_clear_support_needs_space: {{heroA}} (wave clear support) frees up lanes for {{heroB}} (needs space) to scale.

anti.split_push_late: {{heroA}} (split-push/tempo) wants to press the map and end early, while {{heroB}} (late-game scaling) needs the game to go long — conflicting game plans.
anti.deathball_late: {{heroA}} (deathball) is built to group and end fast, pulling against {{heroB}} (late-game scaling), whose payoff is a farm-heavy late game — conflicting timings.

counter.none: This draft has no specialized counters against common threat types (illusions, summons, invisibility, etc.).

summary.high: This team is well-equipped to answer a wide range of common threats.
summary.mid: This team covers some common threats but has notable gaps.
summary.low: This team has little in the way of specialized counters and may struggle against common threats like illusions or invisibility.

pro.none: No professional match data has been imported yet (planned for Milestone 3).

chainLock.name: Chain Lock
chainLock.description: 3+ heroes with strong control chain their disables — +8% to the team's control axis.

ironWall.name: Iron Wall
ironWall.description: 3+ heroes built to survive (durability + saving) — +10% effective survivability in extended fights.

tempoStorm.name: Tempo Storm
tempoStorm.description: 3+ heroes built around early aggression — +12% snowball potential in the first 15 minutes.

oneTrueKing.name: One True King
oneTrueKing.description: Exactly one dedicated Carry, four heroes built to enable them — +6% to the Carry's effective power.

visionWeb.name: Vision Web
visionWeb.description: 3+ heroes with strong map control — +7% map-wide vision advantage.

allMelee.name: All Melee
allMelee.description: Five melee heroes — a frontline wall that trades reach for staying power: +5% durability, -5% skirmish rate, -5% scaling.

allRanged.name: All Ranged
allRanged.description: Five ranged heroes — poke and kite instead of a frontline: +5% skirmish rate, +5% control, -10% durability, -5% map control.

Mana_Booster.name: Mana Booster
Mana_Booster.description: Crystal Maiden's mana aura — allies tagged Mana Dependent get a final-power boost.

Statstealer.name: Statstealer
Statstealer.description: +5% final power to every Statstealer-tagged hero once 2+ are on the team.

Frosty.name: Frosty
Frosty.description: -3% to the enemy team's Movement axis per Frosty hero on this team.

The_Fundamentals.name: The Fundamentals
The_Fundamentals.description: Boosts the team's weakest axis (or axes) — strength scales with how many Fundamentals heroes are drafted.

Two_Heads_Better.name: Two Heads Better
Two_Heads_Better.description: Solo or duo: each doubles their own weakest axis. All 3 (Ogre Magi + Jakiro + Alchemist): replaced by +20% team teamfight and map control.

The_Button.name: The Button
The_Button.description: +5% personal scaling, plus an extra +5% power in the late game — active even solo.

Global.name: Global
Global.description: +10% personal map control, active even solo. 2+ on the team: each also gets +5% teamfight and +5% burst.

Mechanical.name: Mechanical
Mechanical.description: Machines don't tilt — immune to High Skill upset swings and to the opponent's synergy curses.

Healer.name: Healer
Healer.description: Sustained healing keeps the team topped up — adds to team durability, and each Healer contributes more as the group grows.

Gold_Generator.name: Gold Generator
Gold_Generator.description: Feeds the whole team extra gold (Track / Greevil’s Greed) — a richer team scales harder. Adds to team scaling per Gold Generator.

High_Skill.name: High Skill
High_Skill.description: Upsets are more likely around this hero (execution swings the result either way). 2+ on the team: -2.5% overall power each.

Divided_Attention.name: Divided Attention
Divided_Attention.description: -10% personal durability and -10% personal objectives, active even solo — power split across multiple bodies is easier to pick apart.

Tempo_Monster.name: Tempo Monster
Tempo_Monster.description: +3% final power if team tempo > 8; otherwise -25% scaling/durability/map control. Additional -10% if another hard-carry hero is drafted. Never shown to the player.

Summoning_Sickness.name: Summoning Sickness
Summoning_Sickness.description: Summoned units inflate the hero's own calibration. -30% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.

Agility_Crusher.name: Agility Crusher
Agility_Crusher.description: Debuffs enemy agility cores at battle-assessment time. Never shown to the player.

Old_Rivals.name: Old Rivals
Old_Rivals.description: Kunkka and Tidehunter, bound by an old grudge. Forced onto the same team: the tension shows, -5% teamfight each. Facing each other across the draft: whichever of the two is on the enemy side gets personally debuffed, -5% power — the rivalry distracts them even from a distance.

Reunion.name: Reunion
Reunion.description: Mirana and Muerta, reunited. Both on the team: +3% personal map control each.

Unseen.name: Unseen
Unseen.description: Personal invisibility — a real strength no axis measures. +6% personal power, +8% personal map control, active even solo. 2+ on the team: -durability/-teamfight each, scaling with stack count (too many pick-off specialists, not enough frontline).

Army_of_Clones.name: Army of Clones
Army_of_Clones.description: Illusions/clones — extra bodies for damage, split-push, and vision no axis measures. +6% personal power, +8% personal map control, active even solo. 2+ on the team: -durability/-teamfight each, scaling with stack count (the real body is easier to pick apart the more the team leans on illusions).

Mass_Buffer.name: Mass Buffer
Mass_Buffer.description: Team-wide damage amplification (auras/debuffs). Each Mass Buffer hero adds to team teamfight/burst, active even solo — and the per-hero contribution itself grows with stack size (+3% solo, +4% each at 2, +5% each at 3...), so the total scales faster than linearly.

Prone_To_Burst.name: Prone To Burst
Prone_To_Burst.description: Vulnerable to burst damage despite looking sturdy on paper. -20% personal power when the opposing team's raw Burst average is above average.

Disable_Battery.name: Disable Battery
Disable_Battery.description: Backline disable/nuke that wins fights — axes tax these heroes as "dies a lot / farms little," but the real win condition is the battery of control from the fog. +25% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.

Haunt_Absolute.name: Haunt Absolute
Haunt_Absolute.description: Haunt is global presence that axes under-count as personal strength (and Global's map-control buff is inert while that axis weighs 0). +12% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.

Mirage_Tax.name: Mirage Tax
Mirage_Tax.description: Illusion farm and body-count inflate objectives/mobility without a matching real-body fight presence. -15% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.

Paper_Utility.name: Paper Utility
Paper_Utility.description: Utility axes (stacks, map presence, control) read high without converting to outcomes. -25% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.

Raid_Boss.name: Raid Boss
Raid_Boss.description: Late-game / space-dependent cores the mid-clash model under-rates. +18% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.

Showstopper_Tax.name: Showstopper Tax
Showstopper_Tax.description: Flashy initiate/setup reads sky-high on control/tempo without converting in average games. -25% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.

False_Immortal.name: False Immortal
False_Immortal.description: Self-sustain looks like durability on paper; focused burst still deletes them. -18% personal power, always active (stacks with Prone To Burst when that fires). Never shown to the player.

Siege_Voltage.name: Siege Voltage
Siege_Voltage.description: Mid push/nuke cores whose siege and burst win conditions axes under-count. +12% personal power, always active. Never shown to the player.
